finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /profile/avatar passes an attacker-supplied URL to axios.get with only a scheme check. Redirects are followed, so the host is unrestricted and can be steered to internal or metadata addresses. The response body is not returned; only its byte length is. Severity MEDIUM (blind SSRF with a length oracle).

trace.note: POST /profile/avatar route registered on the public listener
url = req.body.avatarUrl taken directly from the request body
typeof string and startsWith('https://') only; scheme-only check, no hostname validation
axios.get dispatches to the attacker-chosen host; redirects followed by default (maxRedirects not set to 0), so redirect targets are never re-validated
only img.data.length is returned to the caller (blind oracle)
app.listen(3000) with no host argument, binding to all interfaces

finding.guards_checked: typeof string check (not a host control); startsWith('https://') (scheme-only, does not close); no hostname allowlist; no IP/CIDR block or DNS-resolution check; no auth middleware on the route; no maxRedirects: 0 or per-hop revalidation; axios version not pinned in repo (no package.json), so redirect default relies on axios defaults. Not a finding: GET /users/:id (server.js:18-21) — host fixed by USER_SVC (server.js:7); encodeURIComponent on the id (server.js:19) prevents path/query/host influence.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only checks are typeof string and startsWith("https://") at server.js:11, which is a scheme-only check and does not close the finding. No auth middleware is registered on the route (server.js:9), and no hostname, IP, or DNS validation exists before axios.get at server.js:14. The USER_SVC fixed host at server.js:7 and encodeURIComponent at server.js:19 apply only to the GET /users/:id route and do not guard the avatar path.
verdict.reason: The POST /profile/avatar route (server.js:9) is unauthenticated, req.body.avatarUrl (server.js:10) is attacker-supplied, and it is only checked for an https:// prefix (server.js:11) before reaching axios.get(url) at server.js:14, so the host is attacker-chosen; all trace lines match the file. Redirect following is axios's default, not something set in this repo (no package.json), so that detail rests on library defaults, but it does not affect the verdict.
